study type: Multi-centre mixed-methods qualitative case study (interviews and focus groups)
cohort: The study included 35 parents (21 women and 14 partners) who had experienced a stillbirth and 22 maternity staff (obstetricians and midwives) from three different maternity hospitals.
finding: There is unacceptable variation in the provision of care after stillbirth, characterized by insensitive interactions between staff and bereaved parents, and a lack of standardized support and communication.
mod_finding: Parents expressed discomfort with staff recommending vaginal birth as the norm and had several unconsidered reasons for requesting a caesarean birth, highlighting a need for better communication and understanding of parents' preferences.
followup_time: N/A (interviews were conducted 'some time ago' after the stillbirth, relying on memory)
cross-section timing: Data was collected in 2013 at three hospitals, with interviews retrospectively gathering parents' experiences of care after stillbirth.
